items.exemplar:
A. Both sides entered expecting a short war, but new rifled weapons and entrenched positions made battles far bloodier and less decisive than anyone imagined.

B. The Confederacy's vast territory meant the Union had to conquer and occupy an area the size of Western Europe while maintaining a 3,500-mile blockade — a task that took four years.

C. Gettysburg and Vicksburg (July 1863) marked the turning point: Lee's invasion of the North failed and Grant seized the Mississippi, splitting the Confederacy.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE reason the Civil War lasted longer than people initially expected.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND reason it lasted so long.
C. Briefly explain ONE important turning point of the war.
items.stimulus: Historian James McPherson notes that Americans in 1861 expected 'a short, glorious war' — yet the conflict dragged on for four years because 'the South's will to resist and the North's need to conquer an entire society made anything swift impossible.'
